$comment: Installer-facing facts for Act 1 and Act 3. anchors are world metres: pole base at origin, Y up, road toward +Z, traffic toward +X.

solar.mount: Pole top or side of an existing pole

battery.placement: External box on the pole; reports health over Bluetooth

coverage.$comment: Two published numbers disagree. widthFt at distFt is Flock's sheet; maxFt and mph are Flock marketing.

flock.label: On Flock’s own pole, with solar power

facts.v: Aluminum, 12 feet tall once installed, 2.875 inches across and 32 pounds; Flock calls it a “DOT breakaway pole”
In dirt, grass or loose gravel; Flock’s crews do not bore through concrete or asphalt
Buried lines are marked through the 811 call-before-you-dig service, and the Flock technician sets up traffic control under the federal work-zone manual (MUTCD)
One on solar power: a second panel would shade the first
Two, 21.25 by 28 inches, 18 to 20 volts and 25.73 pounds with hardware, on top of the pole
$350 to $650 a camera in contracts and quotes from 2022 and 2023. Flock’s 2026 schedule charges $1,000 when a customer changes the agreed plan, and $750 to move a camera on a Flock pole

existing.label: On an existing pole, with solar power

facts.v: 8 to 12 feet; installers work from an A-frame ladder no taller than 14 feet
Adjustable band clamps around the pole, with the solar panels on a bracket at its side
Occasionally required; the customer pays the filing fees, and public works departments may weigh in on the right of way
Where a transportation department controls the right of way, it requires a breakaway pole approved under national crash-test standards (NCHRP 350 or MASH)

$150 a camera on existing infrastructure in a 2023 quote, and $350 to $650 for a standard installation in contracts and quotes from 2022 and 2023. Flock’s 2026 schedule charges $1,000 when a customer changes the agreed plan, and $350 to move a camera on an existing pole

ac.label: On an existing pole, wired to its power

facts.v: An electrician the customer hires connects 120-volt power after Flock mounts the camera
A power kit and a junction box with indicator lights for diagnosis; a replacement kit costs $150
Two can share a pole on wired power
The circuit breaker and the ground-fault protection (GFCI); Flock maintains its own equipment
An intersection bundle of four wired Falcons and two fixed Condor video cameras, listed at $15,000 a year in 2024

solar.label: Solar panels and a battery
solar.summary: Direct current only: the panels charge a battery box, which powers the camera through its rear connector. No cable runs to the ground.

facts.v: Two, 18 to 20 volts, on top of the pole or at its side
A 10.8-volt lithium-ion pack of 19 amp-hours in its own box on the pole; it reports its condition over Bluetooth
One from the panels to the battery and one from the battery to the camera; Flock bills $50 to replace them
No cable carries data; the reads go out over the cellular network (LTE)
The panels’ wattage, how much power the camera draws and how many days the battery lasts

ac.label: Wired power
ac.summary: Power from the customer’s 120-volt supply goes into a Flock junction box, which converts it to direct current for the same rear connector.

facts.v: 120 volts AC, connected by the customer’s licensed electrician
Supplied by Flock, with indicator lights for diagnosis
A replacement AC power kit costs $150; a DC kit is also listed
Only the power source changes; the reads still go out over the cellular network

wing.label: Wing, for an agency’s own cameras
wing.summary: The one setup that uses network cables and fiber. Video from cameras an agency already owns streams to a Wing gateway in its network closet, which reads plates, describes vehicles and sends the results to Flock’s cloud.

facts.v: Wing Gateway 2.0, for 8, 16 or 32 video streams; $300 to $1,000 a year, plus software for each stream
Any network camera that streams video in the common RTSP format, on a network cable that also carries its power (PoE)
Fiber or copper from the switch, through a plug-in module (SFP); then the city’s internet to Flock
Plate and state, or a missing plate; make, type and color; and features such as aftermarket wheels, a roof rack or a trailer hitch
Condor video cameras run on a Flock SIM or on wired power; a solar Condor and a Falcon can share a pole
